evidence.positive: Logged in as loopuser via POST /api/login/basic (session 44ff5419…), GET /api/user/info returned 200 with username loopuser. Ran `update users set enabled=false where username='loopuser'` in the app's Postgres, then GET /api/user/info with the same cookie returned 403; the app log showed `c.g.o.web.auth.DisabledUserLogoutFilter : Ending sign-in session: the signed-in account is disabled or missing` followed by `Unauthorized request: /api/user/info, exception: Full authentication is required`. In Valkey the `spring:session:sessions:expires:<id>` key was gone and the session hash had a 266 s TTL (Spring Session's dying-session grace). Re-enabling the row did not revive the cookie (still 403); a fresh login returned 200. The /websocket filter chain behaves the same: GET /websocket/info with a disabled user's cookie returned 403 with the same filter line. OIDC principal path: generated an OAuth2AuthenticationToken/DefaultOidcUser security context (sub red-sub-1) with the app's own Jackson modules, planted it as a Spring Session hash in Valkey, set loopuser.cognito_sub='red-sub-1'. GET /api/user/info with that SESSION cookie returned 200 as loopuser; after disabling the row it returned 403 with the filter line, and stayed 403 after re-enabling. A planted OIDC session whose sub has no users row (no-such-sub) also returned 403 with the filter line.
evidence.negative: An enabled loopuser session made three consecutive GET /api/user/info calls, all 200, and the count of `Ending sign-in session` lines in the app log did not change. Disabling a different account (`update users set enabled=false where username='admin'`) did not touch loopuser's session: GET /api/user/info still 200, no new filter line; admin was re-enabled afterwards. A disabled loopuser cannot start a new form-login session: POST /api/login/basic returned 401 and the subsequent GET /api/user/info 403.
evidence.red_check: Class swap. Compiled the parent commit's UserService (f83f74b65^) inside the container with javac against /app/jib-classpath-file: @Slf4j written out as an explicit Logger, getCurrentUser without the isEnabled filter, and isSignedInWithoutEnabledAccount()/isWithoutEnabledStoredAccount() returning false so DisabledUserLogoutFilter and DisabledUserStompInterceptor link but never fire (equivalent to them not existing). The pre-fix getCurrentUser logs `PRE-FIX RED CHECK: getCurrentUser served disabled account <username>` whenever it hands back a disabled row. Backed up the shipped class (md5 51c2651569ea5f59767e1c0733b5e45e, copy in scratch), swapped in the pre-fix class (md5 30517f0d33c66ab4415995fbbffbba3c), `docker restart`, waited for readiness. Logged in as loopuser, disabled the row, GET /api/user/info returned 200 with the full loopuser payload on two consecutive requests, and the log carried the PRE-FIX RED CHECK line six times — the bug, red. Reverted: copied the shipped class back (md5 51c2651569ea5f59767e1c0733b5e45e confirmed in /app/classes), restarted, waited for readiness, re-ran login → disable → GET /api/user/info: 403 with the `Ending sign-in session` filter line again. loopuser re-enabled and cognito_sub cleared afterwards.

red_check_signature: PRE-FIX RED CHECK: getCurrentUser served disabled account loopuser
caveats: SSOAuthHandler's own logout-before-redirect was not exercised at runtime: this instance has no identity provider, so the SSO callback cannot be driven. The disabled-user callback case is still caught on the next request by DisabledUserLogoutFilter (shown above with a planted OIDC session), but the 'existing user with no tenant group' branch has no filter-level backstop and rests only on the shipped MockMvc test callbackForExistingUserWithNoTenantGroupEndsTheSession, which drives the real handler and real security filter chain.

The OIDC-principal evidence used a security context planted directly in Valkey rather than one Spring Security saved after a real Cognito login; the JSON was produced by the same Jackson modules SessionConfiguration registers, but authorizedClientRegistrationId 'cognito' was never used by the app in this run.
The disable action was a direct `update users set enabled=false`; the app exposes no admin endpoint for it, so whatever tooling admins use in production was not part of the exercise.

DisabledUserStompInterceptor (STOMP frames on an already-open socket) was not exercised; only the /websocket HTTP filter chain was. Covered by DisabledUserStompInterceptorTest and WebSocketConfigurationInboundChannelTest.
The MGHEpicAuthController refusal of a disabled EHR-launch user was not exercised; covered by MGHEpicAuthControllerTest.

automation.assessment: PR #4837 shipped the coverage with the fix: DisabledUserSessionTest (WebMvcTest with the real SSOAuthHandler and SecurityConfiguration) covers all three acceptance cases — callback for a disabled user, callback for an existing user with no tenant group, and SSO/password/EHR users disabled or deleted while signed in — with callbackForEnabledUserLeavesTheUserSignedIn as the control that proves the 401 assertions can fail; it also covers the websocket handshake. UserServiceTest covers getCurrentUser for enabled/disabled/missing accounts for both principal types, SessionConfigurationUserReloadTest covers the Redis deserializer re-reading the row, DisabledUserStompInterceptorTest covers open sockets, MGHEpicAuthControllerTest covers the EHR launch refusal. All are *Test classes and run in CI. Nothing observed at runtime is missing from that set. A qa-suite end-to-end check was considered and declined: the suite has no database client and the app has no admin API to disable a user, so the test could not flip the enabled flag.

proposed_tests.test: E2E: sign in as a tenant user, disable the account, assert the next GET /api/user/info is 403, with the control that an enabled sibling session on the same run stays 200.
proposed_tests.why_not: Fails bar 1 as a runnable test: qa-suite has no Postgres client (no pg/knex dependency) and the app exposes no admin endpoint that sets users.enabled, so nothing in the suite can disable the account mid-session. Would need an admin user-management endpoint first (a feature ticket, not a coverage branch).

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: After loopuser was disabled mid-session, the next GET /api/user/info returned 403, the DisabledUserLogoutFilter log line fired, and the cookie stayed dead after re-enabling; a planted OIDC-principal session for a disabled account behaved the same way.
Negative: An enabled session kept returning 200 across repeated requests, and disabling a different account did not end it.
Red check: With the parent commit's UserService swapped into the container, a disabled loopuser kept getting 200 from /api/user/info; restoring the shipped class brought the 403 back.

Automation: The MockMvc, service, session and websocket tests shipped with PR 4837 already cover all three acceptance cases with an enabled-user control, so no additional tests are proposed; the SSO callback branches themselves cannot be driven without an identity provider.
